messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGED #oncall (Elena) — Customer Valdora (VPC) reporting large drop in KV prefix hit-rate across dedicated pool 'valdora-prod-1'. Potential customer impact: increased token costs and request latency. Paging severity: P1. Thread started 1950001111.

Elena: I'm on it. Can someone paste the latest kv metrics for that pool?

Tony: seeing it on the dashboards — hit-rate plunged from ~82% to ~6% around 1950000900 UTC. Error spikes: cache-miss amplification and a lot of small keys with same prefix.

Kevin: logs show a sudden surge of unique prefixes from tenant valdora-tenant-42. Likely a client-side prefix fuzzing loop or a warmed-up job that sprayed keys.

Anna: I just heard from Valdora engineering: they rolled a canary yesterday that talked to multiple namespaces for metadata enrichment. They say they didn't change prefix format intentionally but are investigating.

Elena: OK. Mitigation plan: 1) isolate tenant traffic to reduce noise, 2) blacklist/evict the noisy prefix pattern, 3) optionally disable prefix-level caching for valdora-tenant-42 while they fix client. Need volunteers to run evict and routing changes.

Tony: I can run eviction and apply a prefix blacklist rule. Propose: add blacklist pattern: "meta.enrich.*" and soft-evict keys matching "meta.enrich.*" from valdora-prod-1 namespace to restore hit-rate. Command I'll run (samples):
```
# evict matching keys (dry-run first)
kvctl --pool valdora-prod-1 --namespace valdora-tenant-42 evict --pattern "meta.enrich.*" --dry-run
# then run without --dry-run
```

Kevin: Also we should G/scale the dedicated pool by +20% capacity and temporarily route valdora traffic to new nodes if evict doesn't recover latency. I'll prepare a must-gate autoscale now.

Elena: Tony, run the dry-run now and paste results. Kevin, prep scale but hold until we see eviction results. Anna, tell Valdora we're isolating tenant and applying temporary blacklist.

Tony: dry-run returned ~1.2M keys matched and estimated working-set eviction cost = ~18s for streaming eviction. Going to start soft-evict to avoid perf cliff.

Elena: go for it. DeployBot: mark maintenance window for valdora-prod-1 while evict runs.

DeployBot: maintenance ticket created: MV-1950001111, window starting now, TTL 15m.

Tony: running eviction now (no --dry-run). Progress logs: evict batches of 10k — ETA ~3m.

Tony: eviction complete. Immediate metrics: hit-rate jumped to 56% and p50 latency improved from 210ms -> 95ms. Miss amplification reduced.

Elena: good signal. Kevin: please start the +20% nodes as planned for safety.

Kevin: scaling started. New nodes booting, expected ready in ~8m. Routing will split 75/25 until autoscale completes.

Anna: Valdora engineering confirms a bad canary fixed on their side — they reverted the enrichment change. They also provided a client id for the offending job: client-7f9a.

Elena: next steps — medium-term: add per-tenant prefix rate limiting and reactive blacklisting with TTL (automated blacklist for patterns that exceed threshold) to prevent repeat. Short-term: add a protective rule to disable prefix caching for valdora-tenant-42 for 30m while they validate.

Tony: applied 'disable-prefix-cache' for valdora-tenant-42 with 30m TTL. Command: `kvctl --pool valdora-prod-1 --namespace valdora-tenant-42 config set prefix_cache.enabled false --ttl 1800`

Elena: Verified: hit-rate stable ~78% now after scaling and eviction. Latency back to baseline. Marking incident as mitigated but P1 remains until we confirm no customer error pages.

Anna: Valdora reports degraded experience for ~45 minutes but no data loss. They asked for a short incident summary and timeline. I'll draft and send.

SRE-ShiftLead: Good on-the-fly work. Please capture these actions in the postmortem with timestamps: paging -> eviction -> scaling -> disable-cache -> customer revert. Also include proposed action items: per-tenant blacklist automation, prefix-rate-limit, alert tuning for sudden prefix-entropy spikes.

Elena: I'll own the postmortem and draft RCAs. Tagging this thread for postmortem: #postmortems.

IncidentBot: Incident 1950001111 status -> MITIGATED (monitoring).

Kevin: follow-up note — we should add a dashboard panel for per-tenant prefix-entropy and a Cortex rule to page on >50k unique prefixes in 5m for a single tenant.

Tony: logging the exact eviction key count and command in incident ticket MV-1950001111.

Anna: Sent initial customer-facing note. Valdora rep appreciated the quick mitigation and asked for a technical call to review safe practices for enrichment jobs.

Elena: Thanks team. I'll update when postmortem draft is ready. Closing the thread once postmortem link is attached.
